_comment: Validates BINARY PK auto-conversion to VARBYTE. The input defines hash_key as BINARY(500) PK — the connector should create it as VARBYTE(500) in Teradata since BLOB cannot be a primary key. Verifies: table created, PK column is VARBYTE not BLOB, data inserted/updated/deleted correctly.

assertions.name: tester_transaction exists
assertions.sql: SELECT 1 AS x FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM dbc.tablesv WHERE databasename = DATABASE AND tablename = 'tester_transaction') t WHERE t.c <> 1

assertions.name: hash_key column exists and is VARBYTE (not BLOB)
assertions.sql: SELECT 1 AS x FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM dbc.columnsv WHERE databasename = DATABASE AND tablename = 'tester_transaction' AND columnname = 'hash_key' AND columntype = 'BV') t WHERE t.c <> 1

assertions.name: hash_key column is NOT BLOB
assertions.sql: SELECT 1 AS x FROM dbc.columnsv WHERE databasename = DATABASE AND tablename = 'tester_transaction' AND columnname = 'hash_key' AND columntype = 'BO'

assertions.name: tester_transaction has expected row count after upsert+update+delete (2 rows remain)
assertions.sql: SELECT 1 AS x FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM tester_transaction) t WHERE t.c <> 2

assertions.name: hash_key is indexed as primary key (unique primary index)
assertions.sql: SELECT 1 AS x FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM dbc.indicesv WHERE databasename = DATABASE AND tablename = 'tester_transaction' AND columnname = 'hash_key' AND indextype = 'K') t WHERE t.c <> 1
